paper.title_en: The multi-frequency radio light curve of the sub-pc SMBH binary candidate PG 1302-102
paper.abstract_en: Supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) candidates with sub-parsec (sub-pc) orbital separations are rare, high-value systems, thought to be the dominant sources of the recently detected nanoHertz (nHz) gravitational wave (GW) background. Alongside pulsar-timing-array searches for localized nHz GW sources from SMBHBs, an increasing number of candidates have been identified from synoptic surveys of large quasar optical light curves over increasingly long baselines. The optical light curve of the quasar PG~1302-102 at a redshift of $z=0.278$ exhibits a pronounced, smoothly varying periodic signal of ~5.2 years over approximately 20 years. Although the cause of this periodicity remains debated, a plausible explanation is a binary system of two SMBHs with a sub-pc separation. At this close distance, the $10^{8.3-9.4} M_{\odot}$ nuclear black holes in PG 1302-102 are expected to merge within $\sim$$10^{5}$ yr solely due to GW emission. We present a multi-frequency radio light curve analysis of PG~1302-102 spanning a $\sim$19-year baseline, with observations between 2005 and 2024 drawn from the Australian Telescope Compact Array (ATCA). The ATCA radio light curve is highly variable at 5.5~GHz but shows no significant evidence of the periodicity seen at optical wavelengths. However, we report fractionally stronger evidence of periodicity in the in-band spectral index time-series at 5.5~GHz, with a period consistent with the optical periodicity. Furthermore, the recently reported change in optical periodicity is also present in the radio in-band spectral index light curve. These two results suggest that radio and optical periodicity may be physically coupled despite very different emission mechanisms. We argue that this radio-optical coupling reinforces the SMBHB interpretation, despite the optical periodicity change, and provides an intriguing case study ahead of the LSST-SKAO era.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文直接相关于PTA领域，提供了对SMBHB候选体的多频射电观测分析，对理解nHz引力波背景的源具有意义，方法严谨，结果有新颖性。
decision.title_zh: 亚秒差距超大质量黑洞双星候选体PG 1302-102的多频射电光变曲线
decision.abstract_zh: 具有亚秒差距（sub-pc）轨道间距的超大质量黑洞双星（SMBHB）候选体是稀有且价值高的系统，被认为是近期探测到的纳赫兹（nHz）引力波（GW）背景的主要来源。除了利用脉冲星计时阵列搜索来自SMBHB的局域化nHz引力波源之外，越来越多的候选体已经通过基于越来越长基线的活动星系核光学光变的巡天被识别出来。红移$z=0.278$的类星体PG~1302-102的光学光变曲线在大约20年的时间内表现出一个显著的、平滑变化的周期信号，周期约为5.2年。尽管这一周期性的原因仍有争议，一个合理的解释是两颗具有亚秒差距间距的超大质量黑洞组成的双星系统。在这个近距离上，PG 1302-102中质量约为$10^{8.3-9.4} M_{\odot}$的核黑洞预计将仅由于引力波辐射而在$\sim$$10^{5}$年内合并。我们展示了PG~1302-102的多频射电光变曲线分析，该曲线跨越约19年的基线，观测数据来自澳大利亚望远镜致密阵（ATCA）在2005年至2024年间的观测。ATCA射电光变曲线在5.5~GHz处表现出高度变化，但没有显示出光学波段所见的显著周期性证据。然而，我们报告在5.5~GHz的带内谱指数时间序列中存在更强的周期性证据，其周期与光学周期性一致。此外，最近报道的光学周期性的变化也存在于射电带内谱指数光变曲线中。这两个结果表明，尽管发射机制非常不同，射电和光学周期性可能物理上耦合。我们认为这种射电-光学耦合强化了SMBHB的解释，尽管光学周期性有变化，并为LSST-SKAO时代之前提供了一个有趣的案例研究。
